html:
SMTO-DB-0004 — Database access is turned off in this SMTO

GUID: 7e3601ef-af58-4139-82f6-3212c5df41c6
Slug: database-disabled
Domain: DB · Subsystem: db

What happened

  • Whoever set up this SMTO has switched off its database feature, so SMTO won't connect to any database. Nothing was sent to your database.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask the person who manages SMTO whether database access should be on for you, and what you need it for. It was turned off on purpose for the whole installation, so only they can decide to turn it on.
  2. If they agree, ask them to turn database access on and restart SMTO when no Tasks are running. This setting is only read when SMTO starts, so a restart is needed for it to take effect.
  3. After the restart, select New chat and ask your database question again. A new Task picks up the new setting from the start.

What success looks like

  • SMTO answers your database question instead of saying database access is turned off.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't change other limits or safety settings to work around this; only the database access switch controls it.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • NativeSqlCapability.execute refused the request because database_enabled is false in the server's runtime configuration (AOR_DATABASE_ENABLED).

What this means

  • NativeSqlCapability.execute checks database_enabled before resolving or executing the requested SQL. Input rejection is pre-dispatch only where the producer says so. Discovery and psql failures require their original execution evidence; diagnostics do not run SQL or prove that a mutation rolled back.

Why this can happen

  • NativeSqlCapability.execute checks database_enabled before resolving or executing the requested SQL.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the effective database capability configuration and scope before changing query text.

How to fix it

  • database_enabled is read from AOR_DATABASE_ENABLED at server start (default true) and is shown on the Runtime page under Engine and server. If database use is authorized for this installation, set AOR_DATABASE_ENABLED=true in the server's environment and restart the server after active work settles. Change only this setting; leave unrelated timeouts, budgets and policies alone.
  • Ask the operator to enable the database capability for the intended scope if authorized, or use an enabled supported workflow.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • An authorized configuration exposes the capability and its admission check passes.

What not to do

  • Do not change an unrelated timeout, budget or policy. Check whether the named setting applies only to a new task.

Technical notes

  • Input rejection is pre-dispatch only where the producer says so. Discovery and psql failures require their original execution evidence; diagnostics do not run SQL or prove that a mutation rolled back.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
